title: Spelling List 3

words.def: difficult to move because of its size or shape
words.sent: The old couch was so ___ that it took four of us to get it up the stairs.

words.def: to make someone accept as true something that is false
words.sent: He tried to ___ the class into thinking the test had been cancelled.

words.def: goods carried in bulk by truck, train, ship, or aircraft
words.sent: The ___ train was so long that we counted ninety cars.
She painted the hallway a soft ___ so the room would feel bigger.

words.def: a sudden attack of a physical or mental disorder
words.sent: The nurse explained exactly what to do if someone has a ___.

words.def: not the one nor the other of two people or things
words.sent: ___ of the twins wanted to admit who had eaten the last slice.

words.def: a tube of mirrors and coloured glass that shows changing patterns when turned
words.sent: Every twist of the ___ made a pattern nobody had ever seen before.
The film was about a ___ that went wrong in the first ten minutes.

words.def: to lose something, or give it up, as a penalty for doing wrong
words.sent: A team that arrives late has to ___ the match.

words.def: made in exact imitation of something valuable, meaning to deceive
words.sent: The cashier held the note to the light to check it was not ___.
Keep the paint thinner outside — the label says it is highly ___.

words.def: attracting attention by being bold, confident, and full of style
words.sent: His ___ purple jacket could be spotted from the far end of the field.

words.def: a person who lends money in exchange for an item left as security
words.sent: The ___ kept the watch until the loan was paid back.

words.def: inspiring fear or respect by being large, powerful, or very capable
words.sent: Their goalkeeper was a ___ opponent who had not let in a goal all season.

ruleLine: ten of these fourteen words carry an ie or an ei — and the pair is not always where your ear puts it.
